learning_outcomes.text: Know the different types of operating systems, along with their characteristics and capabilities, that can be used as system software in the design and development of a computer system.
Be able to select and evaluate the most appropriate type of operating system to provide a service ensuring the required quality characteristics.
Knowledge of the components and applications that integrate an operating system distribution.
Understand how data structures are used in the management of operating system components and functions.
Know the structure of an operating system.
Understand the basic operating mechanisms of the subsystems that integrate an operating system.
Design and implement applications based on operating system services.
Understand the use of basic parallel and concurrent programming techniques in the operating mechanisms of operating systems.

syllabus_topics: Programming with system calls in UNIX. Implementation of a command interpreter
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum score of 4.5 out of 10 is required for both the theoretical and practical blocks. The final theoretical grade is calculated as (0.5 * T1) + (0.5 * T2). The final practical grade is calculated as (0.4 * P1) + (0.1 * PA1) + (0.4 * P2) + (0.1 * PA2), provided 75% attendance to practical classes is met for each period; otherwise, P and PA grades for that period are zero. If all minimums are reached, the final grade is (0.65 * Theory) + (0.35 * Practices); otherwise, the final grade is the minimum of this formula and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, students may keep theoretical and practical grades of 5 or higher from the ordinary call. A minimum of 4.5 in both the theoretical and practical parts is required, and the final grade is calculated using the same weighted formula as the ordinary call; otherwise, the final grade is the minimum of this formula and 4.0.
